And they now, because they're at war, they have an insatiable need for bronze and where bronze needs tin. Tin is located where the stars are. So, what they're going to do now is build trade routes into these tin places that allow them to extract the tin to create bronze armor. But when they do so, they also create new civilizations and new cities until you get a completely globalized world. China is always at war and needs weapons.

Okay. This is pottery from China during the Shang dynasty, during the Bronze Age. We know it's a completely globalized world because over the past 20 years, we've discovered shipwrecks transporting goods during the Bronze Age. By digging up these ships and analyzing where the products are from, we can rebuild the trade networks.

The green is the copper sources, with many of them. The problem is tin sources are spread out, so to create bronze, you need to constantly expand your trade networks outside. As you can see, expansion keeps going until it encompasses the entire world. Dark brown shows the earliest trade routes and pink later ones. It's always expanding outward to facilitate more trade.

The entire world is encompassed; this includes Britain, Ireland, Scandinavia. The British Isles and Scandinavia are interconnected during the Bronze Age. These areas are major nodes in the trade network because of trade. Red spots are major consumption areas, while gray areas are created to better facilitate trade. Eventually, every source of copper and tin has been discovered with a massive trade network built around each area.

Even though this area is extremely globalized and wealthy, it completely collapses in about 50 years due to the Egyptian records mentioning the coming of sea peoples. These refugees flee famine and team up with pirates who overwhelm existing civilizations including present-day Greece and Turkey. This is a world in complete collapse.

Another map shows these invasions by sea people, just economic migrants or refugees similar to today’s Middle Eastern refugees overwhelming Europe's economic systems. The sea peoples are a mix of different people, and we don't know where they come from or who leads them. Pirates lead the sea peoples, expert at raiding other nations. A painting from Egypt shows the invasions; there were at least three major invasions of sea people with hundreds of thousands attacking at once, leaving Egypt bankrupt.
